prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on your needs (individual vs family, whether you want ACA marketplace plans or off‑market plans, desire for HSA options, budget, need for in‑person help, whether you plan to hire employees, etc.). Instead of a single name, here’s a practical way to find the best broker in Kansas City for a self‑employed person and how to choose among good options.

What to look for in a broker for self‑employed people
- Experience with individual/Marketplace plans and small‑business (SHOP) plans. Self‑employed people often need help with ACA subsidies and plan selection.
- Independence/multiple carrier access. An independent agent who represents many carriers can compare more options than a captive agent.
- Fee transparency. Ask whether they charge a broker fee or work only on commission.
- Knowledge of HSA/HDHPs, telemedicine, and narrow‑network tradeoffs if you want lower premiums.
- Familiarity with state rules (Missouri and Kansas both matter in KC metro) and local provider networks.
- Good communication and availability for year‑round service (not just Open Enrollment).
- Licensing and credentials: confirm they’re licensed in MO (and KS if relevant) and consider NAHU/Certified Insurance Counselor designations.
- References and reviews — ask for a few similar client references.

Where to find brokers in Kansas City
- Local independent insurance agencies: search for “independent health insurance agent Kansas City MO” or “health insurance broker Kansas City.” Independent agencies often serve self‑employed clients.
- National/online brokers that do ACA and individual plans: HealthSherpa, eHealth, GoHealth. They’re convenient and can compare many plans but may be less personal.
- Local professional groups: contact the Kansas City chapter of the National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) or the Independent Insurance Agents of Kansas/Missouri for referrals.
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance website to verify licensing and any complaints.

Questions to ask any broker before hiring
- Do you specialize in self‑employed/sole proprietor clients?
- Which carriers do you represent? Are you independent?
- How do you get paid? Do you charge a fee?
- Can you show me quotes and total expected yearly costs (premiums + typical out‑of‑pocket)?
- Do you help with Marketplace enrollment and subsidy eligibility?
- Will you help year‑round with claims and renewals?
- Can you provide references from current self‑employed clients?

Practical next step
If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether you need individual/family coverage or coverage for employees, your approximate budget, and any doctors or hospitals you must keep in‑network. I can find 3–5 well‑rated local brokers/agents in Kansas City, summarize their specialties, and give contact info so you can contact them and compare.
